subject: Private/VPC deployment pricing — platform fee amortization & support tiers
messages:
From: Jenna Park <procurement@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Zhao <cto@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private/VPC pricing initial questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our procurement team is pulling together commercial options for an on‑prem / VPC deployment and I wanted to surface a few clarifying questions before we schedule the finance call: 

1) Platform fee: can this be amortized over the term (monthly invoicing) rather than an up‑front platform license? If amortization is possible, does Redwood offer a term-based discount (e.g., 3-year vs 1-year)?

2) Licensing metric: are you licensing per-GPU, per-socket, or per-node for the on‑prem package? Do you have example SKU math for a typical 8×A100 footprint?

3) Support tiers: we need a clear mapping of response/restore SLAs and included support hours for Standard vs Premium vs Enterprise. Also: do you include a migration assistance credit for on‑prem (professional services) and how is that priced?

4) SLA credits: what is your approach to service credits for missed latency/uptime targets in Private deployments?

5) Security evidence: we'll also share a security questionnaire — can you attach SOC2 evidence and a sample CSP/confidentiality addendum?

We're aiming to finalize the commercial shape by next week. If you can share a one‑page pricing summary and a ballpark discount range for a 3‑year committed deal, that would be very helpful.

Best,
Jenna Park
Procurement Manager | ACME Corp

Attachments: ACME_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (incoming)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Elliot Zhao <cto@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private/VPC pricing initial questions

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. See answers and an initial commercial sketch below; attaching a one‑page estimate (ACME_Redwood_Private_Pricing_v1.xlsx). Happy to walk through on a call.

Quick summary (high level):
- Licensing: Redwood Private license is priced per‑node for on‑prem with an optional "GPU bundle" per A100 that simplifies purchases. Example: 8×A100 footprint typically maps to 4 nodes (2 GPUs per node) under the common reference architecture; we provide both per‑node and per‑GPU SKUs in the sheet.
- Platform fee: normally invoiced annually as a platform entitlement fee. We can amortize monthly for accounting purposes — commercially we treat amortization as billing timing only (no change to net present value unless there is an explicit discount for multi‑year commitment).
- Term discounts: we offer 8–18% on platform fee for 2–3 year commitments depending on committed capacity and whether billing is annual vs monthly.
- Support tiers:
  * Standard — business hours support, 8×5, 4 business‑hour P1 response, remote troubleshooting; basic updates.
  * Premium — 24×7 with 2‑hour P1 response, incident manager, regular firmware/driver maintenance windows.
  * Enterprise — named TAM, dedicated escalation channel, on‑site assistance options, architecture reviews, and scheduled QBRs.
- Migration assistance: we typically package migration credits as a one‑time professional services credit. For deals with a 3‑year commitment we commonly include 1–4 weeks of migration credits (configurable); larger migrations get custom SOWs.
- SLA credits: we provide SLA credits for platform control plane availability and on‑prem agent heartbeats (not for customer hardware). The credit schedule is in the attachment.

Proposed commercial starting point for ACME (ballpark, subject to final capacity numbers):
- 3‑year term, committed capacity equal to an 8×A100 reference cluster
- Platform fee: $240k/year (listed in sheet) — proposed concession: 15% off platform fee for 3‑year commit (applied to annual platform fee)
- License: per‑node license at listed rate — proposed 10% first‑year discount on license line for multi‑year commit
- Migration credit: 2 weeks equivalent (one‑time) included

If ACME needs an up‑front platform fee instead of amortized billing, we can provide both options in the final quote; amortized monthly billing will be listed as a payment timing preference.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in Ben Carter (Sales Lead) and Marissa Cole (Enterprise AE) to confirm discount authority and finalize a draft commercial.
- Can we set a procurement deep‑dive on Tuesday 5/5?

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_Private_Pricing_v1.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private/VPC pricing initial questions — commercial guidance request

Ben/Marissa — forwarding the thread with Jenna (ACME procurement). They are asking for an amortization option on platform fee and an aggressive migration credit request. Key points and decision items: 

- They want the platform fee amortized monthly; that is fine operationally but procurement cares about net concession.
- I sketched 15% off platform for 3‑year commit + 10% on license first year + 2 weeks migration credit. Jenna will push if they can get more.
- Ask: What is the max platform fee concession we can offer before we need VP approval? Also: can we extend migration credit to 4 weeks if they sign a 3‑year enterprise package (Enterprise support tier)?

Inline from Ben (below) — pls confirm:

On 2026-05-04 09:34, Ben Carter wrote:
> Olga — thanks for the draft. For ACME (strategic account + likely to request a Dedicated/Private roll‑out across multiple teams), recommend the following commercial play:
>
> * Platform fee concession: up to 18% on the annual platform fee for a 3‑year firm commitment if they agree to Enterprise support and a $350k committed ARR floor. Anything above 18% requires VP approval.
> * License discount: 12% first year if we get a 3‑year term; 8% recurring thereafter (we can phase).
> * Migration credit: we can stretch to 4 weeks but require them to accept Enterprise support and a 60% prepayment for year 1 (or equivalent escrow).
>
> I'll standby for the pricing worksheet updates and can join the call on Tuesday.
>
> — Ben

Ben — can you confirm whether the prepayment / escrow requirement can be softened (ACME indicated capex constraints). If not, we'll present the 15%/10% as the conservative option and escalate only if they push.

Thanks — Olga

From: Jenna Park <procurement@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Zhao <cto@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private/VPC pricing initial questions

Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround and for pulling Ben in. We ran this internally with finance and technical ops. A few items from our side: 

- Term: ACME is prepared to do a 3‑year term if the commercial offset is adequate.
- Platform fee concession: we can accept 15% but would prefer 18%.
- Migration credit: we can accept 2 weeks if we get 18% on platform fee; otherwise we need 4 weeks.
- Support tier: we are prepared to take Enterprise if it includes named TAM and two on‑site half days during the first 90 days.
- Prepayment: finance is reluctant to prepay 60% for year 1. Can we instead agree to a 30% upfront deposit with milestone invoicing tied to delivery?

If you can confirm final commercial terms (platform fee with percent concession, license pricing, migration credit, support addenda) we can route to legal for redlines. Please include a DocuSign link for signatures and provide the SOC2 evidence link for our security team.

Best regards,
Jenna Park
Procurement Manager | ACME Corp

Attachments: ACME_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx
